entries.title: Ian Happ’s 1,000-hit milestone reminds of championship-chasing Cubs’ connection to World Series era
entries.summary: <p>When <b>Ian Happ</b> made his big league debut, the champagne had been soaked up, the confetti swept away and Grant Park changed back into a summer playground after serving as party central the previous November.</p><p>But the guys Happ called his teammates on his first day with the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> were the ones who broke the curse. And though those guys are long gone by now, Happ’s still here.</p><p>He’s never stopped being a Cub. And despite a potential end to his time with the organization on the horizon – he’s due to hit free agency at season’s end – everyone got a reminder of Happ’s 10-season tenure Wednesday, when fans showered him with cheers after he picked up his 1,000th career hit.</p><p>“Man, a lot of hits, a lot of time in this stadium with these fans,” Happ said after the game. “That’s what makes it so special, just being with this team for as long as I have, wearing this uniform, representing the city … and the tradition of what’s here.</p><p>“To do it with one team, to do it over the course of my career here, that’s what makes it really, really cool.”</p><p>Happ ranks 37th on the franchise’s all-time hits list. And while no one is ever taking the mantle of “Mr. Cub” from the guy who ranks second, <b>Ernie Banks</b>, if that was a rotating title, Happ would have a great argument for owning it.</p><p>He’s spent a decade in the home clubhouse at Wrigley Field, serving as a connection to the group of players who achieved what was once unthinkable: bringing a World Series championship to Clark and Addison.</p><p>That’s not nothing, not when these Cubs are trying to accomplish the same.</p><p>“Ian’s extremely proud of his time here. And he’s connected to the previous generation, kind of the only guy,” manager <b>Craig Counsell</b> said Thursday. “There’s a sense of history from that. It’s recent history, I guess, but it’s still history. And I think that matters, and I think that’s important.</p><p>“He’s eager to talk about it, and I love that because I think we should all be eager to talk about history, I think we can learn so much from it. That’s a cool thing.”</p><p>Happ’s time alongside <b>Anthony Rizzo</b>, <b>Jon Lester</b> and the rest turned him into the player he is today. And now he’s taking the turn for a new generation of Cubs.</p><p>“To come up with the guys that I did and that group of individuals, players who have accomplished so much in the game, to watch the way that they played and the way they went about their business and the things that they’ve achieved and kind of continue that on here,” Happ said. “I played with guys who have set some crazy records here.</p><p>“To be able to be on some of those lists, it’s special to me, means a lot.”</p><p><b>Cabrera ready to rock</b></p><p><b>Edward Cabrera</b>’s time away from the Cubs’ rotation comes to an end Friday, when he starts against the Giants.</p><p>Cabrera has been out for more than two weeks while dealing with a blister on his finger.</p><p>It’s a big deal for a rotation that’s dealt with plenty of injuries early, <b>Cade Horton</b> done for the season and <b>Matthew Boyd</b> – who is set for a second rehab start Saturday – missing a month.</p><p>“Maybe the rest can do him some good,” Counsell said. “It can do him some good, freshen him up and get him ready for the next four months.”</p>

entries.title: Redemptions for Pete Crow-Armstrong, Dansby Swanson as Cubs return to walk-off ways: ‘This is who we are’
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> were heading for rock bottom Thursday night.</p><p>It sure looked like an ugly stretch was about to get uglier, with Pete Crow-Armstrong making a rare fielding gaffe in center and Shota Imanaga tagged for four home runs.</p><p>A loss would have taken them to last place in the NL Central, by the smallest of percentage points, an unthinkable landing spot for a team with championship-level expectations.</p><p>But then, joy.</p><p>The Cubs rallied from a 6-1 deficit to score a comeback 7-6 win, walking off the A’s and avoiding a sweep at Wrigley Field.</p><p>“Whenever you get to run and jump around like little kids,” Crow-Armstrong said, “it’s always a blast.”</p><p>Who else but Crow-Armstrong would be in the middle of everything?</p><p>After he lost a fly ball that dropped behind him and went for an inside-the-park home run – a play that seemed to represent everything that’s gone wrong for the Cubs the last few weeks – he immediately found redemption with a homer of his own.</p><p>“The first time it’s happened to me here. Pretty helpless feeling,” Crow-Armstrong said of the defensive miscue. “But it’s about moving on. There’s not much you can do about that except hope you see it next time.</p><p>“In the past, I might have dwelled on that, and that always ends up affecting how you go about the rest of your day. People having my back, me not hiding from the next at-bat, I’m growing up a little bit and proud of that.”</p><p>Three innings later, Crow-Armstrong also delivered the game-winning knock, an RBI single that capped a conga line of a ninth inning that saw a previously sputtering Cubs offense score four runs on seven hits.</p><p>“We’ve stayed in the fight all year. And we’ve been fighting through these last couple weeks,” Crow-Amrstrong said. “This kind of stuff is exactly what we’re capable of.”</p><p>The Cubs didn’t necessarily view Thursday’s outcome as a way to rinse the bad taste of a 5-18 stretch from their mouths but rather as a reminder that, hey, this team can be pretty good.</p><p>This kind of thing was commonplace earlier in the campaign, with the Cubs winning six of their first 37 games in walk-off fashion. The previous one came May 6. Two days after that, the Cubs were 15 games north of even on a 10-game winning streak. And then?</p><p>Well, let’s just say the Cubs would like this to be their normal once again.</p><p>“This is who we are,” shortstop Dansby Swanson said. “For the last three weeks, we’ve not been that. So for everyone to get [to see], ‘Hey, this is what we’ve been talking about, this is what we’ve been working toward, this is what this group is capable of,’ to have that show up in so many different ways, from so many different guys in the lineup … that’s what this group is about.</p><p>“For us to come through and get that win is not only something we can build off of but the reminder that this is who we are. That’s so important when times are like this.”</p><p>Swanson, who’s been the biggest target for frustrated fan complaints thanks to the .183 batting average he carried into Thursday, got his own moment of redemption, delivering a two-out RBI single that tied the game in the ninth.</p><p>Wrigley went nuts, but no one was going crazier than Swanson, who was screaming and pumping his fist at first base, perhaps celebrating a monkey-free back?</p><p>“I’m most happy for Dansby, obviously,” manager Craig Counsell said. “It’s been rough. But he came up big, and it was a huge hit and a really good at-bat.</p><p>“He’s fired up we won, but I think there was a little bit of that other thing in there, too, no doubt about it.”</p><p>Swanson was happy, too, that he was trusted to deliver in that situation, not pinch hit for like he was late in Tuesday’s game.</p><p>“No,” Counsell said, asked if he considered making a move. “It was Dansby’s at-bat.”</p><p>With so many Cubs redeemed Thursday night, is this the end of it? Have the Cubs cathartically put this sorry stretch behind them and turned their season around?</p><p>“You never know,” Crow-Armstrong said. “You’ve just got to wait and see.”</p><p>“That’s too big a statement for me. We’ve got to come and play a game tomorrow,” manager Counsell said. “Hopefully we tell that story in October.”</p>

entries.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams on 'she-wolf' Myles Garrett, his Michael Jordan tribute and his video game cover
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> quarterback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/06/03/bears-caleb-williams-madden-27-cover-revealed-quarterback-video-game-nfl-ea-sports" target="_blank" >Caleb Williams</a> has another edge rusher to worry about. Or at least he hopes so, come playoff time.</p><p>The Bears don’t have the Rams on their schedule this year. If they play at all, it would have to be a rematch of last season’s playoff thriller. But there’s no question the Bears took notice this week when the Rams, already a Super Bowl favorite, traded for Browns edge rusher Myles Garrett.</p><p>Garrett has a case to be the greatest defensive player ever dealt in his prime. Williams showed the edge rusher respect Thursday by referencing Roman history — or maybe a Shakira song.</p><p>“Another she-wolf in the NFC,” Williams said during EA Sports’ Opening Drive event at the tip of Navy Pier. “So we’ll hopefully see him at the end of the year, since he’s not on the schedule. Hopefully not. But if we do, it means we’re in the playoffs and we’re rolling. So super excited. Good for them.”</p><p>Did he think the Bears would sign a free agent edge rusher this offseason?</p><p>“As you know, it’s not my realm … ” he said before invoking Montez Sweat and Austin Booker. “We’re expecting big things from them. We obviously last year got a couple guys [in Dayo Odeyingbo and Shemar Turner] that are wanting to be in the position to step up and make plays for us. That’s what we’re waiting on, that’s what we’re wishing for.”</p><p>Williams saw one of his wishes come true this week when he was revealed as the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/06/03/bears-caleb-williams-madden-27-cover-revealed-quarterback-video-game-nfl-ea-sports" >cover subject for Madden 27. </a></p><p>Thursday, he was introduced to a crowd of influencers and made podcast appearances while EA Sports unveiled a Madden mini-movie that featured actor Vince Vaughn taking over as GM of the Bears. In a surreal few hours, Williams chatted with former players Cam Newton, Michael Vick and Chad Ochocinco as college mascots from Iowa, Wisconsin, Florida, Texas Tech and Syracuse plodded by in puffy shoes. Williams’ parents were there — and so was teammate Rome Odunze.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/bqQtZ9xm_uI?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen title="Madden 27 | Official Reveal Trailer | EA SPORTS"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p>The excitement surrounding Williams and the Bears felt like a post-modern version of the Bears’ convention in 2019, when former players declared the team Super Bowl contenders. The Bears have to hope this season better lives up to expectations.'</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr"><a href="https://x.com/hashtag/Bears?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#Bears</a> QB Caleb Williams faces Cam Newton in <a href="https://x.com/EAMaddenNFL?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@EAMaddenNFL</a> <a href="https://t.co/5UFOX6LM0g">pic.twitter.com/5UFOX6LM0g</a></p>— Patrick Finley (@patrickfinley) <a href="https://x.com/patrickfinley/status/2062709986480758893?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">June 5, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>The video game has two separate covers — Williams making a jump throw and, on the deluxe version, him rubbing his arms in his “Iceman” celebration. EA Sports wanted a cover with the jump throw. Williams said putting it in front of the Chicago skyline was his idea. He wanted to pay homage to the famous photo of Michael Jordan dunking with the skyline in the background.</p><p>Williams didn’t think he was being too bold in making the comparison. It was a tribute to Jordan, who he’s working on meeting up with soon.</p><p>“It was more of a respect thing, bringing retro back, not letting people forget that, and doing it on my side of the world of football,” he said. “Paying respect to that and him and what he was able to do in Chicago.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Caleb Williams on <a href="https://x.com/EAMaddenNFL?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@EAMaddenNFL</a> : <a href="https://t.co/bQYBXYvKkQ">pic.twitter.com/bQYBXYvKkQ</a></p>— Patrick Finley (@patrickfinley) <a href="https://x.com/patrickfinley/status/2062693733036867844?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">June 5, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Williams has never been afraid to make big plans. Before he was drafted, he famously said he wanted to surpass Tom Brady’s seven Super Bowl rings. When he plays video games, he picks the Bears so he can be the quarterback himself.</p><p>Being the first Bears player ever put on the main cover of “Madden” is part of that journey, he said, but not the destination. </p><p>“It’s another small steppingstone to tell me to keep going, that I’m going in the right direction …” he said. “I’m in the position I want to be in and I’ve got the people around me, from coach to teammates … [and] my support system to also remind me to keep going. This wasn’t the end-all, be-all goal for me. …</p><p>“I’ve got some big goals.”</p><p></p><p></p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" entries.summary: <h2>Moon Alert</h2> <p>Avoid shopping (except food and gas) and important decisions after 2 p.m. The moon is in Aquarius.</p><h2>Aries (March 21-April 19)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Listen to the advice of someone older or more experienced because this could be beneficial for you. Nevertheless, you might get in a dispute with a friend or a member of a group about money, possessions, or financial matters. Perhaps the cost of something? Stay chill.</p><h2>Taurus (April 20-May 20)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-4d0000" name="html-embed-module-4d0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>An <b>average</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Tread carefully today because you might find yourself at odds with a parent, boss or someone in authority, including the police. (Never underestimate the power of courtesy.) With fair Venus in your house of communications, you can talk your way into and out of anything.</p><h2>Gemini (May 21-June 20)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Steer clear of controversial subjects — politics, religion and racial issues — because this is the classic day for an argument with others. In fact, some people are just itching for a fight. On the other hand, this is a great day to make travel plans or discuss legal matters.</p><h2>Cancer (June 21-July 22)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-4d0000" name="html-embed-module-4d0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>An <b>average</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Money squabbles and issues about shared property, taxes and debt might arise today. Or perhaps the disagreements are about shared expenses. Fortunately, relations with authority figures are excellent. In fact, someone with clout might benefit you today.</p><h2>Leo (July 23-Aug. 22)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> For the most part, this can be a favorable day for you; however, you might be at odds with a partner, spouse, friend or someone in authority. Don't ruin your day with this kind of squabble. It's a popular time for you. Enjoy the company of others.</p><h2>Virgo (Aug. 23-Sept. 22)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Don't get your belly in a rash about issues related to politics, religion, foreign countries, or legal matters because there is very little you can do right now. However, people will be inclined to listen to you if you want to share your ideas because you look good to everyone.</p><h2>Libra (Sept. 23-Oct. 22)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Work-related discussions about budgets, expenses and financial matters will go well today. However, issues related to other countries, the law, medicine and politics might create conflict with someone. Tread carefully. Take baby steps. Don’t make a big deal about anything.</p><h2>Scorpio (Oct. 23-Nov. 21)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Be patient with family members today, including partners, spouses and close friends, because arguments can arise easily. This is because the moon is in Aquarius at odds with fiery Mars. Fortunately, family discussions can be practical and productive.</p><h2>Sagittarius (Nov. 22-Dec. 21)</h2> <p></p> <div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-7b0000" name="html-embed-module-7b0000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>positive</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p> Avoid work-related squabbles or arguments related to your health or a pet because they will only drain your energy and you don’t need this. Instead, this is an excellent day to plan artistic projects, social events, vacations, sports and fun times with kids. entries.title: Madden 27 trailer features Vince Vaughn as Bears GM — and eventually Caleb Williams' replacement at QB
entries.summary: <p>Ryan Poles is out as <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> general manager, and Vince Vaughn is in.</p><p>That's the comedic premise of EA Sports' trailed for the upcoming Madden 27 video game that features Bears quarterback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2025/08/31/why-do-so-many-people-hate-bears-qb-caleb-williams-he-answers-exactly-that-question" >Caleb Williams</a> on the cover. Williams and Vaughn shot parts of the four-minute video at Halas Hall, including a scene in which Vaughn pushes a "Previous GM" nameplate off the desk and replaces it with his own.</p><p>"My first decision: Lock down my franchise QB," Vaughn said leading into a scene in which he negotiates a contract extension with Williams followed by a montage of game play.</p><p>Vaughn also introduced a new nickname for Williams: "Permafrost." It's a veiled joke about the legal battle over him trying to trademark the nickname Iceman.</p><p>Williams gave an odd look at the camera as Vaughn said, "We've done the focus groups, we've done the straw polls. They love it. It's 'Permafrost.'"</p><p>Vaughn took a FaceTime call from retired quarterback Tom Brady in which Brady begged him for a spot as Williams' backup, which Vaughn rejected. It was another layered joke since Brady turned down the Bears in 2020 in favor of signing with the Buccaneers.</p><p>The trailer also featured cameos by the Packers' Micah Parsons, the Rams' Matthew Stafford and others.</p><p>It wrapped with Vaughn transitioning into a dual role as GM-coach, then adding quarterback to his job description at age 56 and saying at a news conference, "It's important to get this out of the way: The rumors are true. I'm the coach, I'm the GM and now I'll be playing quarterback... Caleb's supportive. We're going to have a spot for him. But I think he's just loving watching me play quarterback. We're a team. Everyone puts the team first, and that's why I'm running everything."</p><p>Here's the full video:</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Run the league one decision at a time.
